title: Every licensed child-care centre and the public money attached to it
question: Which licensed centres does public money reach, through which stream, and how many take more than one?
finding: San Francisco had 400 open child-care centre licences with 20,650 places on 8 November 2026; 26 more licences with 1,329 places were pending, many of them replacing a closed licence at the same address, and 20 with 3,172 places were inactive. Of the open licences, 202 centres (9,949 child places) are on the City's list of funded centres, 126 centres (6,747 child places) belong to an operator holding a State child-care or preschool contract, 31 centres (1,090 child places) sit at a Head Start address and 147 centres (7,674 child places) at a federal meal-programme site; 160 centres draw on two or more of these and 124 on three or more, while 157 centres (7,895 child places) show none. By kind of operator: nonprofit 170 centres (8,782 child places, 113 centres in the City network); private company 70 centres (3,601 child places, 31 centres in the City network); corporation, tax status not found 47 centres (2,403 child places, 7 centres in the City network); public body 31 centres (2,439 child places, 24 centres in the City network); church or religious body 26 centres (1,692 child places, 6 centres in the City network); not determined from the records 25 centres (1,091 child places, 11 centres in the City network); individual licensee 16 centres (493 child places, 4 centres in the City network); small centre, 14 places or fewer 15 centres (149 child places, 6 centres in the City network).
how: One row per open centre licence in the State licensing file (family homes excluded; a site with an infant and a preschool licence has two rows). A licence is marked as City-funded when its number is on the Department of Early Childhood's list of Early Learning For All centres (177 sites, page dated 2025-06-11); as a meal site when the State's current meal-programme list has a site at its address; as Head Start when the federal locator lists funded places at its address. State contract, facilities grant and City payment columns are operator totals, repeated on each of the operator's rows: State general child-care and preschool contract maximums for 2025-26, grants named on the Low Income Investment Fund's tax returns for 2021 to 2025, and what City early-childhood departments paid the operator directly in fiscal 2026. Kind of operator comes from the licensee name, the City payment file and a name match to the federal list of tax-exempt organizations. Rows are ordered by number of streams, then places; 15 centres licensed for 14 or fewer children are counted but not listed.
limits: A centre with no stream shown may still be paid: City and State vouchers follow a family to any provider, are paid through two referral agencies, and no list of the centres paid is published. The City publishes which centres are in its network but not what each is paid, how many places it funds or how many children are enrolled. A State contract belongs to the operator, not to a site, so it is attached to all the operator's centres. Several streams at one centre is how the programmes are built: the City's own subsidy includes a "gap" payment for families already receiving State or federal subsidies, as the Controller's 2019 audit describes. Kind of operator is inferred from names and can be wrong. Citations are as the State lists them, mostly for the last three to five years. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days.
